newsitem.title: FRANCE: Boeing merger seen speeding up Airbus changes.
newsitem.headline: Boeing merger seen speeding up Airbus changes.

text.p: A European Union decision Wednesday to approve Boeing Co.'s $15 billion acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp. could be a blessing in disguise for the European Airbus Industrie consortium, analysts said.
The decision could convince the four Airbus partners to speed up their own merger, they said.
The European Commission, the EU's executive body, gave its approval after Boeing, in last-minute talks, dropped its intention to sign exclusive contracts with airlines.
Boeing dropped its intention to have exclusive supply contracts with AMR Corp.'s American Airlines, Continental Airlines Inc. and Delta Air Lines Inc.
The analysts said Airbus will have to do two things to secure its future in the ultra-competitive airline market, where orders are picking up this year after about five meagre years.
The consortium must become a real company and secure financing for its A-3XX "superjumbo" airliner project, the analysts said.

Toulouse-based Airbus Industrie is made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain.
Aerospatiale and Deutsche Airbus have 38 percent each. British Aerospace Plc has 20 percent and CASA 4 percent.

The four companies and the governments of the member countries have agreed that Airbus should become a proper company with its own balance sheet. However, the companies still disagree about which assets to transfer to Airbus, and at what price.

The A-3XX, a project that could cost up to $12 billion to develop, will be a very large plane that would finally allow Airbus to win orders in a market segment where Boeing has a virtual monopoly with its 747 jumbojet.
Boeing has dropped its own plans to develop a very large plane, leaving the field for the moment to the Europeans.
